en: The Sūtra on the Mahāprajāpatī’s Parinirvāṇa, translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazang of Henan during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Vatsala, traveling along the Monkey River.

At that time, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī was traveling through the kingdom of Vṛji with five hundred bhikṣuṇīs; all were arhats and possessed great supernormal powers. These included Cundā, Mahāprajāpatī, Viśākhā, Utpalavarṇā, and Bhadrakāpilānī—these being the senior bhikṣuṇīs who were her great disciples—and they were staying at a bhikṣuṇī monastery in the kingdom of Vṛji.
At that time, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī thought to herself:
"I cannot bear to see the Buddha enter parinirvāṇa, along with Ānanda, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana—these worthy ones. I shall first relinquish my life-force and enter nirvāṇa."
At that time, the Buddha, having already perceived this, spoke to Ānanda:
"In this place, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī thought to herself:

'I cannot bear to see the Buddha enter parinirvāṇa, nor can I bear to see the venerable ones—Ānanda, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana. Therefore, I shall first relinquish my life-force and enter nirvāṇa.'"

"These five hundred bhikṣuṇīs, having awakened in their own minds, have abandoned all suffering. We cannot bear to see the Buddha enter parinirvāṇa, nor can we bear to see such venerable ones as Ānanda, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana; we too shall relinquish the formations of life and depart into nirvāṇa."
The Buddha spoke thus. Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“For this reason, my body cannot support itself; I cannot distinguish the various directions, nor can I recognize for myself the Dharma I have heard.”
"Why is this? Because it has been heard that Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī is about to enter parinirvāṇa.
The Buddha then addressed the venerable Ānanda:
"Thus it is, Ānanda!
Consider this for yourself:

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī maintains the lineage of diligence and has entered parinirvāṇa; she also maintained the dharmas of the lineages of concentration, loving-kindness, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of deliverance—those which I myself have known, realized, and awakened to, whether they be the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold path of wisdom. Do you fear that Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has departed, taking these dharmas with her?"
When the Buddha had finished speaking these words, Ānanda said to him:

“Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī will ultimately be unable to maintain the lineage of purity and pass into parinirvāṇa; she will also be unable to maintain the lineage of concentration, the lineage of wisdom, the lineage of liberation, the lineage of the knowledge and vision of liberation, and she will ultimately be unable to maintain the lineage of awakening.”

Regarding the dharmas realized through the Buddha’s own wisdom—whether they be the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, or the eightfold path of noble wisdom—he ultimately cannot maintain these dharmas in parinirvāṇa.

Ānanda said: "I myself reflect that Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has rendered great kindness to the Buddha; when the Buddha’s mother passed away, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī nursed and raised the Buddha until he grew up."
The Buddha said:
"Ānanda, there is such a thing."
“Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has been exceedingly kind to me; when my mother passed away, she nurtured me with her milk and raised me to adulthood.
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!”
I, too, have bestowed immeasurable kindness upon Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī. Why is this?

It is because, through my causal conditions, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has taken refuge in the Buddha, taken refuge in the Dharma, and taken refuge in the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus; she has practiced the path to its completion, and no longer doubts the Buddha, no longer doubts the Dharma, no longer doubts the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus, and no longer doubts the practice of the path to its completion—all these she has fully understood.

"Ānanda, if a person can teach others to take refuge in the Buddha, to take refuge in the Dharma, to take refuge in the Saṅgha of bhikṣus, to take refuge in those who have practiced the path to its end, and to receive [the precepts] for as long as life lasts; and if they further provide them with food, clothing, bedding, and medicine, never refusing what they seek, and continue thus for the duration of their lives—even so, they would still not yet have been able to repay the debt of gratitude to their teacher."
The Buddha said, "Therefore,
Ānanda, I have bestowed immeasurable and boundless grace upon Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī."

At that time, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, together with five hundred bhikṣuṇīs, went forth from the kingdom of Vaiśālī and arrived among the great trees. Reaching the place where the Buddha was, she prostrated herself with her head at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to stand to one side; those five hundred bhikṣuṇīs likewise prostrated themselves before the Buddha and stood to one side.
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī then joined her palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I cannot bear to witness the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, nor that of the venerable bhikṣus Ānanda, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana; I wish to first relinquish my life-force and attain nirvāṇa."
Having reported this matter thus, the Buddha accepted Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī’s report by remaining silent.
Then Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī rubbed the Buddha’s feet with her hands and said:

“Today is the last time I shall see the one upon whom the world relies; today is the last time I shall see the light of the world; today is the last time I shall see the unsurpassed one in the world. From this day forward, I shall no longer see the Honored One within the three realms.”
Having prostrated themselves before the Buddha, they withdrew and sat to one side.
Those five hundred bhikṣuṇīs likewise joined their palms and addressed the Buddha in this way:

“We cannot bear to see the Buddha enter parinirvāṇa, nor the venerable Ānanda, Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, and the other venerable bhikṣus. We wish to relinquish our life-faculties and attain parinirvāṇa.”
The five hundred bhikṣuṇīs addressed the Buddha in this manner, and the Buddha accepted what the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs had said by remaining silent.
Then the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs bowed their heads at the Buddha’s feet and said:

“We shall see the refuge of the world for the last time; we shall see the light of the world for the last time; we shall see the unsurpassed one of the world for the last time. From this day forward, we shall no longer behold the Honored One within the three realms.”
Having spoken thus, they each returned to their seats.

After the Buddha had finished preaching various discourses on the Dharma for Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs, they all rose from their seats with joy. They paid homage to the Buddha, circumambulated him three times, and prostrated themselves with their heads to the ground. Then they returned to the kingdom of Vaisālī and entered the Bhikṣuṇī Vihāra in the Royal Garden. There, they arranged five hundred seats in one place; Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs each took their respective seats.

At that time, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, manifesting her own supernormal powers, vanished from her seat and departed. Emerging from the east, she stood in mid-air; rising from one tree to seven trees, she displayed four supernormal powers while walking back and forth in the sky.

Having walked, she would stand; having stood, she would sit; having sat, she would lie down; and having lain down, she manifested five-colored flames from her body: five-colored flames issued from her upper body while water issued from her lower body, and five-colored flames issued from her lower body while water issued from her upper body.

In this manner, he vanished from the east and appeared in the west, and vanished from the south and appeared in the north; then, descending from between the seven trees to the ground, he manifested supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) just as before, and immediately extinguishing those powers, he entered *nirvāṇa*.

At that time, the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs all vanished from their seats and emerged from the east, remaining in mid-air. They ascended from the height of one tree to the height of seven trees, manifesting the four grades of supernormal power (*ṛddhipāda*) by walking back and forth in the sky;

having walked, they stood; having stood, they sat; having sat, they lay down; and having lain down, they emitted five-colored flames from their bodies—five-colored flames from the upper body while water issued from the lower body, and five-colored flames from the lower body while water issued from the upper body.

In this manner, they vanished from the east and appeared in the west, and vanished from the south and appeared in the north. Then, descending from the height of seven trees to the ground, they manifested transformations and supernormal powers as before, whereupon they extinguished those powers and entered *nirvāṇa*.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda:

"Go tomorrow at dawn to the kingdom of Vaiśālī and go to the house of Cāpāla. Once you have arrived, inform Cāpāla that the Buddha’s mother has entered parinirvāṇa, along with five hundred bhikṣuṇīs. The Buddha exhorts you, Cāpāla, to prepare five hundred biers, five hundred jars of sesame oil, five hundred portions of incense, and five hundred portions of firewood, as well as various kinds of flowers and perfumes and various kinds of musical instruments, and bring them to the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃghārāma in the Royal Garden."

Why is this? The Mother of the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa along with five hundred bhikṣuṇīs; they were all arhats possessed of great supernormal powers, whose merits were already complete, and they ought to be given a proper funeral.
The Buddha said to Ānanda, “Inform the householder Kāla that the Buddha exhorts him thus.

Having heard the Buddha’s words, Ānanda replied, “So be it,” and immediately rose, prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet in salutation. He then departed at dawn for the kingdom of Vaiśālī, went to the residence of the householder Yeta-Kāla, and upon arrival, addressed the gatekeeper:
"Please inform the householder that Ānanda is outside.
When the gatekeeper heard Ānanda’s words, he immediately went inside and reported this.

At that time, the householder Yeta was on a high tower, amusing himself with female entertainers; hearing the gatekeeper’s report, he was instantly terrified, his hair standing on end. He immediately descended from the tower and went out to meet Ānanda. He then placed his head at the feet of the Venerable Ānanda as a mark of respect and said to him:
"This is neither ordinary nor a minor matter.
Why is this so? Venerable one, why have you entered the kingdom so early?"
Yatākarāvatya said, "What is your intention?
Ānanda immediately replied:

"The Buddha has sent me here, wishing to exhort you, Kāla-vaṃśa, to prepare five hundred sedan chairs, five hundred jars of sesame oil, five hundred portions of incense, and five hundred portions of firewood, as well as various kinds of fine perfumes and flowers and various kinds of musical performances, and bring them to the Bhikṣuṇī-vihāra in Rājaka."

Why is this? The Mother of the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa along with five hundred bhikṣuṇīs; they were all arhats possessing great supernormal powers, and their merits were already complete. They ought to be given a magnificent funeral.
"The Buddha exhorted the householder Kāla in this manner.
When the householder heard Ānanda speak thus, he immediately fell prostrate on the ground in a swoon and said, "Worthy Ānanda!"
"What fault have I or my people committed against the bhikṣuṇīs?
What grievance do the bhikṣuṇīs have toward me or my people,
that they did not inform me or my people of their parinirvāṇa?"

"Venerable Ānanda! From this day forward, the walking hall shall be empty; the seats shall be empty; the places for walking meditation shall be empty; the crossroads, streets, and alleys shall all be empty; indeed, the entire kingdom of Śrāvastī shall be empty."
Venerable Ānanda!
From this day forward, we shall no longer see bhikṣuṇīs traveling through the country of Vaiśālī; how grievous this is!

When Yeta Karava had finished speaking, Ānanda addressed the householder, saying: "The Buddha himself has previously declared that all affectionate attachments must inevitably end in separation and dispersal;

each shall go to a different place and each shall follow a different path. Whatever is born, wherever one arrives, and whatever one conceives—all have their own courses and their own causes and conditions. They will surely perish and they will surely part; it is ultimately impossible to prevent such separation. Therefore, a person of wisdom should simply protect the practice of the Dharma."

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, for the sake of the householder Kāla, cited various sūtras to clarify and interpret his intentions and to exhort him; having thus clarified, gladdened, and exhorted him, he then proceeded to the kingdom of Veṣālī.

The Brahmins and householders of Vaiśālī were gathered together in the lecture hall. When the Venerable Ānanda had arrived and taken his seat, he addressed the Brahmins and householders of the country of Vaiśālī:

"Gentlemen, prepare five hundred couches, five hundred jars of sesame oil, five hundred portions of incense, and five hundred portions of firewood; also prepare various kinds of fine perfumes and flowers, and various kinds of music. Bring these to the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃghārāma in Rājaka."

Why is this? The Mother of the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa along with five hundred bhikṣuṇīs; they were all arhats possessing great supernormal powers, and their merits were already complete. They ought to be given a magnificent funeral.
The Buddha exhorted the brahmins and householders in this manner.
Then the brahmins and householders of Śrāvastī threw themselves upon the ground and said to the Venerable Ānanda:
"What fault have we committed against the bhikṣuṇīs?"
"What grievance do the bhikṣuṇīs have against us?
By what failure have they offended the bhikṣuṇīs' minds that they did not inform us before entering parinirvāṇa,
O Venerable Ānanda?"
From this day forward, the halls shall all be empty; the seats shall all be empty; the crossroads and the lanes and alleys shall all be empty; only the kingdom of Śarīra shall be considered empty.
"From this day forward, I shall never again see a bhikṣuṇī entering the country of Vaiśālī to beg for alms.

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the brahmin householder of Vaiśālī: "The Buddha has previously declared himself that all affection and love must inevitably end in separation and dissolution;

each shall go to a different place and follow a different path. Whatever is born, wherever it goes, and whatever it conceives, each has its own course and its own causes and conditions. One must inevitably part; though one desires not to part, it can never be avoided. A person of wisdom should simply protect the practice of the Dharma."

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, for the sake of the brahmin householder of the village of Veṭhadīpa, cited various essential sūtras to explain the intent of the brahmin householder, to gladden his intent, and to encourage his intent. Having thus explained, gladdened, and encouraged him, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat and went to where the Buddha was.

At that time, the householder Yeta, together with five hundred brahmin householders, took five hundred litters, five hundred jars of sesame oil, five hundred portions of firewood, five hundred portions of incense, and various kinds of fine perfumes, flowers, and music, and proceeded to the Bhikṣuṇī-vihāra at King’s Garden. Upon their arrival, the gate of the Bhikṣuṇī-vihāra at King’s Garden was closed; thereupon, the householder Yeta addressed one man, saying:
"Come, climb onto another's shoulders, cross over the wall into the garden, and open the gate."
The man accepted the householder’s words, climbed onto another man’s shoulders, crossed over the wall, and opened the gate.
The householder Yajñadatta and five hundred brāhmaṇas together entered the Bhikṣuṇī-vihāra in the royal park.
At that time, five hundred bhikṣuṇīs had six śrāmaṇeras as their attendants. These six śrāmaṇeras said to the householder Yajñadatta:
"Venerable householder!"
Do not harass these five hundred bhikṣuṇīs. Why is this?
For they are all those who have attained meditative concentration and are seated in it.
At that time, the householder addressed the six śrāmaṇeras, saying:
"These five hundred bhikṣuṇīs did not give rise to a concentrated mind; they have already relinquished the activity of life and attained nirvāṇa."
At that time, having heard these words, the six śrāmaṇeras immediately fell prostrate on the ground in a faint, saying:
"Who will ever again instruct us? Who will ever again admonish us?
Following whose footsteps shall we carry our robes and bowls?"
At that time, the householder addressed the venerable six śrāmaṇeras, saying:
"The Buddha previously declared himself that all who are bound by affection must inevitably part."
"The wise novice Rāhula need not grieve; he should simply practice diligently and increase his vigor.

At that time, the householder Anāthapiṇḍada took the relics of Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and, with various kinds of incense, flowers, and music, reverently collected the relics and placed them upon a golden bed. He did the same for the relics of the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍada, together with five hundred brāhmaṇa householders, took the relics of Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and those of the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs and went to where the Buddha was.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra:
"Come! Turn toward the true east with palms joined, kneel on your right knee to the ground, and speak thus:"

"Those who dwell in the eastern direction—who possess upright faith and upright conduct, and whose great supernormal powers and merits of the three insights and six knowledges are already perfected—all come to this place."

Why is this? The Mother of the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, as have five hundred bhikṣuṇīs; they were all arhats possessed of great supernormal powers, whose merits were fully perfected, and we ought to provide them with a magnificent funeral.
"It is the same in the south, the same in the west, the same in the north, and the same in the east.
Having received these words, the Venerable Śāriputra immediately turned toward the east, the south, the west, and the north to invite the Arhats.

Immediately, three hundred and fifty arhats came from the east; likewise from the south, likewise from the west, and likewise from the north, so that a total of one thousand arhats were gathered before the Buddha.
The Buddha, together with a community of one thousand bhikṣus, went to the site of the śarīra of Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī; the Buddha then sat down, and the thousand bhikṣus all took their seats.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Arise, take the relics of Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, place them in a bowl, and bring them here to put into my hands."
Ānanda replied, “So be it.
He then rose from his seat, took the śarīra of Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, placed them in his bowl, and presented them to the Buddha; the Buddha then received them with both hands.
When Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī had received her portion of relics, the Buddha addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:

"This is the aggregate of relics belonging to a woman. Originally she possessed an evil body—fickle, coarse, violent, light-minded, and frequently shifting with envy—but Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has already cast off this female aggregate of a body; that which is to be attained by a man, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has already attained."

At that time, the Buddha instructed Yaśoda Kātyāyana and the assembly of bhikṣus to jointly erect a stūpa for Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs. Once the stūpa had been erected, the people of the kingdom of Vaiśālī, as well as all devas and humans, together honored the stūpa of Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī and the five hundred bhikṣuṇīs.
When the Buddha had spoken thus, all the bhikṣus rejoiced; they rose, prostrated before the Buddha, and departed.
This concludes the *Mahāprajāpatīparinirvāṇa Sūtra* as spoken by the Buddha.
